title: Strings
theory:
### Text as immutable sequences

`str` holds Unicode code points; normalize encoding concerns at I/O boundaries
(decode bytes early, encode late). Strings are immutable: “changing” one builds a
new object. `str.join` is the idiomatic way to concatenate many fragments without
quadratic copies.

### Formatting

f-strings (`f"{value:!r}"`) are the default readability win. `str.format` and
`Template` remain useful for localization pipelines or user-supplied patterns where
you want different safety trade-offs.

```python
parts = ["hydro", "electric"]
label = "-".join(parts)

ratio = 0.125
assert f"{ratio:.1%}" == "12.5%"
```

exercises.title: String Constants
exercises.description: Declare a string variable greeting and assign it the value "Hello, Python!". Then print it using print.
hints: Preserve the greeting variable exactly as seeded in starter (including embedded punctuation), then print it.

exercises.title: Using Runes
exercises.description: Declare a rune variable and assign it the Unicode character for 'A'. Print it using both %c and %d verbs to see character vs code point.
hints: ord(ch) emits Unicode codepoints for length-1 str objects.
Two labeled print lines recreate sample stdout.

exercises.title: String Manipulation
exercises.description: Use strings.Contains to check if "Hello" is in "Hello, World!", strings.Replace to replace "World" with "Python", and strings.Split to split "a,b,c" by comma.
exercises.expected_output:
Contains: true
Replaced: Hello, Go!
First: a
hints: Coerce booleans via str(...).lower() before printing textual true.
replace swaps substrings once; split breaks CSV-like tokens.
exercises.solution:
text = "Hello, World!"
print("Contains:", str("Hello" in text).lower())
print("Replaced:", text.replace("World", "Go", 1))
print("First:", "a,b,c".split(",")[0])

exercises.title: String Formatting
exercises.description: Use print to format a string with a name and age, then print it. Also use printf to format a floating point number to 2 decimal places.
exercises.expected_output:
Alice is 30 years old
Pi is 3.14
hints: f"{name} is {age} years old" covers the prose line.
exercises.solution:
name, age, pi = "Alice", 30, 3.14159
print(f"{name} is {age} years old")
print(f"Pi is {pi:.2f}")

exercises.description: Given s = "hello", reverse it by converting to list or string reversal, swapping characters, and converting back. Print the reversed string.

exercises.description: Declare url = "https://example.com". Check if it starts with "https://" and ends with ".com". Print both results.
hints: Use in for embedded checks and lower-case textual booleans to match stdout.
